scenario.summary: The Interlock ransomware group has introduced a PHP-based Remote Access Trojan (RAT) variant, delivered via the KongTuke campaign using social engineering and malicious PowerShell scripts. The malware establishes a command-and-control channel through Cloudflare Tunnels and fallback IPs, performs extensive host and domain reconnaissance, and maintains persistence via registry run keys to facilitate lateral movement through RDP.

meta.rationale: Focus the search on standard user endpoints first. If no activity is found on the trycloudflare subdomains, broaden the search to look for any process executing from AppData\Roaming\php\.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has maintained access using a PHP-based RAT persisting via registry Run keys and is moving laterally through the environment using RDP.

blind_spots.remediation: Audit unmanaged assets and install agents on all user workstations.

blind_spots.risk: RDP connections without authentication context can be misidentified; an automated script vs an interactive logon is a critical distinction.

blind_spots.remediation: Configure enhanced RDP logging to include logon types in sign-in events.

hunt.name: Interlock PHP RAT: Persistence and Lateral Movement
hunt.description: This hunt targets the late-stage behavior of the Interlock PHP RAT, specifically looking for the execution of PHP interpreters from user-writable AppData paths, persistence via registry Run keys loading encrypted .cfg files, and anomalous internal RDP traffic indicative of lateral movement. It also examines network telemetry for Cloudflare Tunnel C2 activity and fallback connections to hardcoded IP addresses.

config.scoping_notes: Focus the search on standard user endpoints first. If no activity is found on the trycloudflare subdomains, broaden the search to look for any process executing from AppData\Roaming\php\.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule on registry Run keys is easily bypassed by changing paths. This hunt correlates process execution from writable paths, specific registry patterns, Cloudflare tunnel usage, and fallback IP connections into a single triage session, providing a multi-surface context no single rule can offer.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\roaming\php\%.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%php%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wefs.cfg%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%config.cfg%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts running PHP interpreters from non-standard user profile paths, a hallmark of the Interlock PHP RAT deployment.
config.expected_signal: A PHP process running from a user profile directory loading a configuration file. Silence means no PHP binaries matched these specific command-line strings.

primitive_config.label: PHP execution from AppData Roaming
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\roaming\php\%.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%php%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%wefs.cfg%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%config.cfg%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A PHP process running from a user profile directory loading a configuration file. Silence means no PHP binaries matched these specific command-line strings.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, reg_target, reg_value_data, time FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\currentversion\run%' AND LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%php.exe%' AND LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%.cfg%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the registry entry used to maintain access after reboots.
config.expected_signal: A Run key entry pointing to a PHP binary and a .cfg file in AppData. This matches the known persistence mechanism.

primitive_config.label: Registry Run-key persistence for PHP
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, reg_target, reg_value_data, time FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\currentversion\run%' AND LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%php.exe%' AND LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%.cfg%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A Run key entry pointing to a PHP binary and a .cfg file in AppData. This matches the known persistence mechanism.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.trycloudflare.com' AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%php%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%powershell%'))) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify process-driven DNS requests to the trycloudflare.com domains named in the report.
config.expected_signal: Specific trycloudflare subdomains being resolved by PHP or PowerShell. Silence means these domains were not queried.

primitive_config.label: DNS queries to Cloudflare Tunnels

primitive_config.expected: Specific trycloudflare subdomains being resolved by PHP or PowerShell. Silence means these domains were not queried.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE instr(',' || '{{fallback_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Check for network activity to hardcoded fallback IPs that bypass DNS entirely.
config.expected_signal: Connections to fallback IPs. Any such row is highly suspicious as these IPs have no legitimate business purpose in most networks.

primitive_config.label: Direct connections to fallback IPs
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE instr(',' || '{{fallback_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Connections to fallback IPs. Any such row is highly suspicious as these IPs have no legitimate business purpose in most networks.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) AS connection_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE dst_endpoint_port = 3389 AND direction = 'outbound' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip HAVING connection_count <= 5 ORDER BY connection_count ASC
config.description: Identify rare RDP lateral movement targets that differ from standard administrative patterns.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts making infrequent RDP connections to internal peers. Common admin jumps will have high counts; lateral movement will likely be a rare pair.

primitive_config.label: Stacking internal RDP connections

config.objective: Determine if any host exhibits a combination of PHP profile execution, registry persistence for that PHP binary, and outbound C2 or anomalous internal RDP connections.
config.description: Analyze the process execution, persistence, C2 traffic, and RDP patterns to identify compromised hosts.
config.expected_signal: A verdict for each host involved in the queries, identifying whether they match the Interlock variant's behavior.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign with a justification citing specific rows from at least two different surfaces.

config.question: The triage verdict identifies at least one host as 'malicious' with multiple corroborating surfaces.

config.description: Direct the response based on the agent's confidence in the compromise.
Contain the threat by removing the host from the network.
config.instructions: Isolate the host immediately. Do not reboot. Prepare for forensic imaging of the AppData directory and registry hives.

config.description: A human analyst reviews the findings to confirm the RAT variant and identify potential lateral movement targets.
config.instructions: Review the agent's triage notes. Specifically, verify the rare RDP destinations identified. Determine if the .cfg files are consistent with Interlock's encryption format.
Document the findings. If malicious activity was found, pivot to Incident Response. If not, consider adding trycloudflare.com lookups from user profiles to your standing detection rules.
